conceptGroups.concept: Self-reported race and/or ethnicity or ancestry/ethnic origin (select all that apply, with free-text option)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Race and/or Ethnicity: Captures the self-reported racial and/or ethnic identity of the participant, answering 'How would you describe your race and/or ethnicity or ancestry/ethnic origin?' Answer type is a combination of structured categorical selection (select all that apply) from a standardized value set — including American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black or African American, Middle Eastern, North African, Native Hawaiian or Pacific Islander, White or Caucasian, and Other — plus an optional free-text field for specific ancestry or ethnic origin detail (e.g., Italian, Haitian, Cherokee, Korean). Source is self-report. The concept spans both broad racial categories and specific ethnic/ancestral origins, and the ideal CDE accommodates multi-select (check all that apply) as the primary response mode, with a single best-fit option as an alternative summary, and a free-text write-in for granular ancestry.

Diastolic blood pressure measurement: 'What is the diastolic blood pressure?' Numeric value in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), integer or decimal. No single qualifier is uniformly specified across member fields; fields carry reading-instance qualifiers (first reading [bp1], second reading [bp2]), indicating this CDE may need to be instantiated per measurement occasion. No laterality, posture, or subject qualifier is consistently specified in the source fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Family history of specific cancer type: which biological relatives have been diagnosed (per cancer type)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Family history of cancer by cancer type and biological relative: For each specific cancer type (e.g., bladder cancer, blood/soft tissue cancer, bone cancer, brain cancer, breast cancer, and other cancer types), identifies which biological family members have been diagnosed with that cancer. The question asked is 'Who in your family has had [cancer type]? Select all that apply.' Answer type is a multi-select checkbox allowing simultaneous selection of one or more biological relatives from a fixed set of options: Mother, Father, Sibling, Daughter, Son, Grandparent (and potentially other relatives). Each cancer type is captured as a separate item, and each response is a set of zero or more relative-type values. No laterality, body-site sub-qualifier, or time-window qualifier is specified; the subject is the participant's biological family members (not the participant themselves).

Diastolic blood pressure measurement: 'What is the diastolic blood pressure?' Numeric value in millimeters of mercury (mmHg), integer or decimal. No single qualifier is uniformly specified across member fields; fields carry reading-instance qualifiers (first reading [bp1], second reading [bp2]), indicating this CDE may need to be instantiated per measurement occasion. No laterality, posture, or subject qualifier is consistently specified in the source fields.

conceptGroups.concept: Neighborhood walkability perception: multi-item self-report scale (aesthetics, sidewalk presence, sidewalk maintenance, daytime crime safety, nighttime crime safety, traffic, physical activity visibility) rated on 4-point Likert agreement scale
conceptGroups.idealCde: Neighborhood walkability perception: a multi-item self-report instrument assessing the respondent's perceived walkability of their own neighborhood across key domains including aesthetic appeal (interesting things to look at), sidewalk presence, sidewalk maintenance/condition, and daytime and nighttime walking safety related to crime. Each item is answered on a 4-point Likert agreement scale (1=Strongly disagree, 2=Somewhat disagree, 3=Somewhat agree, 4=Strongly agree) with additional response options for 'Does not apply to my neighborhood,' 'Don't know/Not sure,' and 'Prefer not to say.' The unit of measurement is ordinal agreement rating per item; items may be summed or averaged into a composite walkability perception score. Qualifier: self-report about respondent's own residential neighborhood.

Body composition and weight status assessment: a cluster of measures capturing (1) calculated Body Mass Index (BMI, kg/m²), (2) measured body weight in kilograms (numeric/text entry), (3) DXA-derived assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water from AGC scan (decimal, %), (4) DXA-derived assumed percentage of lean body mass that is water from WBC scan (decimal, %), and (5) self-perceived weight status (categorical: Overweight | Underweight | Just about right). Together these fields answer: 'What is the participant's body size, body composition, and self-assessed weight status?' Answer types range across calculated numeric (BMI, kg/m²), continuous numeric (weight, kg), decimal percentage (DXA LBM water fraction, %), and ordinal categorical (self-perception: 1=Overweight, 2=Underweight, 3=Just about right). Note: DXA water-in-LBM fields carry distinct scanner/protocol qualifiers (AGC vs. WBC), and the self-perception field is self-reported by the participant.

Educational attainment (self-reported): the highest grade, level of schooling, or academic/vocational degree or diploma the respondent has completed or received. Answers the question: 'What is the highest grade or level of school you have completed, or the highest degree, certificate, or diploma you have obtained?' Expected answer type: ordinal categorical, encoded as a single ordered scale spanning no formal schooling through advanced post-secondary degrees, with categories covering: (1) never attended / kindergarten only; (2) elementary grades 1–8; (3) secondary/high school grades 9–12 without diploma; (4) high school diploma or equivalent (e.g., GED); (5) some post-secondary without credential; (6) trade/vocational certificate or diploma; (7) non-university college diploma (e.g., community college, CEGEP); (8) bachelor's degree; (9) graduate or professional degree (master's, doctorate, professional). No laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier is present; the subject is the respondent (self). Units: none (categorical ordinal).

conceptGroups.concept: Average number of cigarettes smoked per day (current or historical)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Average daily cigarette consumption: captures the typical number of cigarettes smoked per day, either currently or over the lifetime smoking period (fields span both current and historical/average-over-entire-smoking-period contexts). The question asks: 'On average, how many cigarettes do/did you smoke per day?' Answer type: numeric integer (count of cigarettes per day), with 20 cigarettes equaling 1 pack as a reference unit; may be collected as a free-text number entry or ordinal range (e.g., 1–10, 11–20, 21–30, 31–40, 41–50, >50); permissible non-numeric responses include 'Don't know' and 'Prefer not to answer'. Note: member fields carry two distinct time-window qualifiers — current daily cigarette count and average daily cigarette count over the entire past smoking history — which should be treated as separate CDEs if time window precision is required.

conceptGroups.concept: Visual acuity letter score and LogMAR under mesopic and photopic conditions for each eye (OD and OS)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Visual acuity measured separately under two luminance conditions (mesopic low-luminance and photopic standard-luminance) for each eye individually (right eye [OD] and left eye [OS]); answers the question 'What is the patient's visual acuity under mesopic and photopic conditions for each eye?'; recorded as both a raw letter score (integer count of letters read correctly, text entry) and a derived LogMAR score (continuous calculated value in LogMAR units); qualifier: laterality (OD vs OS) and luminance condition (mesopic vs photopic) are both required dimensions of the CDE.

conceptGroups.concept: Typical number of drinks per week by beverage type (beer, liquor, red wine, white wine, other) on weekdays vs. weekend days in the past 12 months
conceptGroups.idealCde: Alcohol consumption by beverage type and day type (weekday vs. weekend) during the past 12 months: captures the typical number of drinks consumed per week of a specific alcoholic beverage (beer, liquor, red wine, other alcohol) on weekdays or weekend days in a typical week over the prior 12-month period. Question: 'In a typical week during the past 12 months, how many drinks of [beverage type] do you drink on [weekdays / weekend days]?' Answer type: non-negative decimal (number of drinks), with separate values per beverage type (beer, liquor, red wine, other alcohol) and per day-type stratum (weekdays, weekend days); time window qualifier: past 12 months.

conceptGroups.concept: Specific cancer type(s) diagnosed (per site: bladder, breast, colorectal, lung, etc.) as binary indicators or coded type
conceptGroups.idealCde: Cancer diagnosis history: a binary indicator of whether the participant has ever received a physician diagnosis of cancer (any type). Answers the question: 'Has a doctor ever told you that you had cancer (of any type)?' Expected answer type: categorical/boolean (Yes / No / Prefer not to say). Companion CDE(s) should capture specific cancer type(s) diagnosed (e.g., bladder, breast, colorectal, etc.) as separate binary indicators or a multi-select field per cancer site.

conceptGroups.concept: Current employment status (categorical, multi- or single-select)
conceptGroups.idealCde: Current employment status of the participant (self-reported). Answers the question: 'What is your current employment status?' Captures the participant's present work/labor-force situation at the time of assessment. Expected answer type: categorical (select all that apply or single-select), with response options covering at minimum: Employed for wages (full-time), Employed for wages (part-time), Self-employed, Out of work/unemployed less than 1 year, Out of work/unemployed 1 year or more, Unemployed less than 6 months, Unemployed 6 months or more, Homemaker, Student, Employed on leave (health-related), Employed on leave (non-health-related), Retired and not working, Retired and working, Retired and volunteering. No laterality, body-site, or condition qualifier; subject is the participant (self). Time qualifier: current (at time of data collection).

Help us learn more by completing this survey about your neighborhood, social life, stress, and feelings about your everyday life. This survey will take less than 10 minutes to complete. diff.rawDescription: The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at
diff.cleanedDescription: The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at
diff.embedText: The English Indices of Deprivation 2010 are measures of multiple deprivation at the small area level. The model of multiple deprivation which underpins the Indices of Deprivation 2010 is based on the idea of distinct domains of deprivation which can be recognised and measured separately. These domains are experienced by individuals living in an area. People may be counted in one or more of the domains, depending on the number of types of deprivation that they experience. Each domain represents a specific form of deprivation experienced by people and each can be measured individually using a number of indicators. Seven distinct domains have been identified in the English Indices of Deprivation; Income Deprivation, Employment Deprivation, Health Deprivation and Disability, Education Skills and Training Deprivation, Barriers to Housing and Services, Living Environment Deprivation, and Crime. Individual domains can be used in isolation as measures of each specific form of deprivation. They can also be combined, using appropriate weights, into a single overall Index of Multiple Deprivation which can be used to rank every small area in England according to the deprivation experienced by the people living there. Along with two supplementary indices, Income Deprivation Affecting Children Index and Income Deprivation Affecting Older People Index, they form the English Indices of Deprivation. These statistics allow the most, and least, deprived areas of the country to be identified as well as providing information about the issues faced by people living in different parts of the country.

diff.cleanedDescription: peak to peak time in milliseconds A digital volume pulse can be considered to be
diff.embedText: peak to peak time in milliseconds A digital volume pulse can be considered to be the summation of a direct and a reflected component. The direct component is due to transmission of a pressure wave from the left ventricle to the finger via the most direct route. The reflected component is formed by pressure transmitted from the heart to the lower body where it is reflected back up the aorta and thence to the finger. peak to peak time is the difference between the peak values of direct and reflected components.
